title: Microsoft Teams: organisers play OneDrive videos in events with Manage what attendees see
summary: The briefing accurately separates the roadmap's meeting-and-event scope from Microsoft's narrower event rollout notice. No actionable contradiction was found; minor corrections concern the template locking step, a missing citation for OneDrive sharing permissions, and a permissions recommendation not represented in the controls table.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the new preloaded OneDrive video feature itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams OneDrive preloaded video; OneDrive video Manage view; Teams OneDrive preloaded video events Manage view permissions playback licensing price meter clients. Read plan-events and events-licensing; results describe VOD, recordings and Clipchamp, not this option.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how file permissions are checked for playback to event attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: Manage what attendees see OneDrive video permissions. Read manage-meeting-presentation-experience and collaboration-options; search excerpts cover embedded Outlook/Loop videos and meeting recordings, not permissions checks for this event playback.

claims.claim: With Manage what attendees see, organisers must intentionally bring shared content and video on screen.
claims.quote: Organizers must intentionally bring shared content and video on screen before attendees can see it.

claims.claim: Manage what attendees see lets organisers control on-screen content and whose video is visible.
claims.quote: When this option is enabled, meeting organizers can control what content is shared on screen and who's video is visible.

claims.claim: Learn does not say whether OneDrive video uses the same explicit bring-on-screen step.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive video Manage view; Manage what attendees see OneDrive video permissions. Read manage-meeting-presentation-experience and plan-events; neither describes the new OneDrive video's staging sequence.

claims.claim: The notice describes human selection and playback controls, not autonomous actions.
claims.quote: Organizers and producers will be able to select and share videos stored in OneDrive directly within Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see and will have access to built-in controls to start and pause video playback during events.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this new Manage view video option appears on clients beyond Desktop and Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams OneDrive video events Manage view web mobile client supported. Read roadmap and events-platform-support search excerpts; web support for Manage what attendees see in smaller events does not specify support for this new video option.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting templates > Add > Meeting engagement > Manage what attendees see reaches the custom template setting.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, expand Meetings and select Meeting templates. ... Select Add. ... To prevent the meeting organizer from changing an option, select the option and then select lock.
claims.fix: The printed path reaches the option but stops before locking it. Keep the path for its default value and add to the note: 'To lock the setting, select Manage what attendees see, then select lock.'

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented to set or lock Manage what attendees see inside a custom meeting template.
claims.quote: Searched: TeamsMeetingTemplate Set Manage; TeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration PowerShell update set; Manage what attendees see Graph template. Read Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration (read only); Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy excerpts set visibility/default template, not its options.

claims.claim: Custom meeting templates require Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Meeting settings in sensitivity labels and custom meeting templates require Teams Premium.

claims.claim: The use of custom meeting templates for events optimized for scale is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events optimized for scale custom meeting templates Manage what attendees see default OneDrive video. Read create-custom-meeting-template, custom-meeting-templates-overview and plan-events; prebuilt town hall/webinar event templates do not establish custom meeting template applicability.

claims.claim: A custom meeting template can set the default value of Manage what attendees see.
claims.quote: Default value - This is the value that's applied to a meeting when the template is used. ... Manage what attendees see | When On, meeting organizers can preview and approve content being shared on screen before other meeting participants can see it.

claims.claim: A template can lock the option so the organiser cannot change it.
claims.quote: Lock status - This determines if the meeting organizer can change the option that was set by the template. If the option is locked, the meeting organizer can't change it.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No admin policy on either UI or automation is documented for organisers choosing Manage what attendees see in events.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Manage what attendees see events admin policy PowerShell custom meeting template set Graph API. Read plan-events: 'Manage what attendees see | No control.' Read Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax; no parameter sets this option.

claims.claim: The presentation-experience page gives no admin policy for Manage what attendees see, but does give template and organiser control.
claims.quote: | Setting | Admin policy | Sensitivity label | Template | Meeting organizer | ... | Manage what attendees see | No | No | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: OneDrive sharing permissions remain a control over access to the file itself.
claims.quote: When users share a file or folder, they can choose from several types of sharing links that offer different levels of permissions. ... Specific people links require the user to specify a list of people who will have access to the file or folder.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/collaboration-options for the sentence 'OneDrive sharing permissions on the file remain the existing control over the file itself.' Add that URL to sources; do not claim it establishes attendee playback permissions.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: No control specific to OneDrive video in events is described in Learn at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Manage what attendees see OneDrive policy; Teams OneDrive preloaded video events Manage view permissions playback licensing price meter clients. Read plan-events, manage-meeting-presentation-experience and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; no switch or video-selection restriction for this option.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to ensure appropriate OneDrive file permissions, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Ask producers to store videos in OneDrive with the appropriate permissions before using them, as the notice advises. ... Default and lock of Manage what attendees see in a custom meeting template ... Admin policy for organisers using Manage what attendees see in events
claims.fix: Remove the 'Ask producers to store videos in OneDrive with the appropriate permissions before using them, as the notice advises' bullet from Governance guidance. Keep the notice's permissions recommendation in the existing explanatory prose; do not add a control row.

controlChecks.governs: Default and lock of Manage what attendees see in a custom meeting template
